0.label: figure_with_tapper_over_ring
0.description: A small frontal figure with a round head standing in the central channel, holding a long rod whose end reaches down into the notched ring below (#1).
0.iconography: Read with the ring, a diviner striking a tray with a tapper (ìróké) — the gesture that opens an Ifá consultation. Otherwise a figure holding a staff of office.

1.label: compartmented_ring
1.description: A circle whose border is divided into about ten segments with toothed edges and small ovals in some compartments, centred in the channel; the rod from #0 enters it from above.
1.iconography: It looks like a miniature ọpọ́n Ifá seen from above — a compartmented rim around an empty centre — with the tapper touching it. Alternative readings: a coiled serpent, a beaded ring or a drum-head. The segment count is a small 'pattern as number' test.

2.label: s_scroll_side_band
2.description: The full-height right-hand band of running S-scrolls, framing the central channel.
2.iconography: Right half of the scroll frame that encloses the scene (see #6).

3.label: hafted_blade
3.description: A small T-shaped object with a flared blade on a short handle, at the lower left of the channel beside the palm (#4).
3.iconography: An axe or hoe — a tool of Ògún (iron) or an offering; with #5 part of a set of implements at the foot of the scene.

4.label: oil_palm
4.description: A plant with a straight stem and a fan of five or six pointed leaves, at the foot of the central channel between blocks.
4.iconography: Most likely the oil palm — the tree of Ifá, whose nuts (ikin) are the diviner's instruments. With the ring and tapper above, it makes this panel an Ifá scene.

5.label: paddle_or_club
5.description: A small club- or paddle-shaped object with a rounded head, at the lower right of the channel.
5.iconography: A tool or offering object paired with the blade (#3); possibly a mallet, paddle or spoon.

6.label: s_scroll_side_band
6.description: The full-height left-hand band of running S-scrolls, mirror of #2.
6.iconography: Left half of the scroll frame. Scrolls rather than plait: a different frame idiom from its sister plank (panel 01).

7.label: intimate_couple_with_snake
7.description: Two nude frontal figures side by side at the top of the channel, one reaching to the other's body, a wavy serpent at their left and a tall plank-like object at their right.
7.iconography: A couple — fertility and marriage, as on the Ifá tray EBA-Div_00302 — with a serpent beside them (earth, renewal). The panel places them above the divining scene: the question put to Ifá.

8.label: wavy_serpent
8.description: A thin wavy line running down the left edge of the channel beside the couple.
8.iconography: A snake, the serpent of #7 — continuity and threshold power.

9.label: implements_at_the_base
9.description: The lower compartment as a whole: blade, palm and club set among rectangular blocks at the foot of the channel.
9.iconography: An offering ground or shrine: tools and the palm of Ifá laid out below the consultation.

panel.title: Ife board: a couple, a diviner at the tray, and the palm of Ifá
panel.object_type: carved board (door leaf or shrine panel)
panel.summary: A board with two full-height scroll bands enclosing a central channel. Top to bottom: a nude couple with a serpent; a figure whose long rod touches a compartmented ring; and an oil palm with tools at the base.

register_readings.reading: A couple and a serpent — the matter of marriage and fertility.
A figure strikes or points into a compartmented ring — likely a diviner with tapper and tray.
The oil palm of Ifá with a blade and a club among blocks — the diviner's tree and offerings.
The S-scroll bands that frame the whole.

panel.composition: A framed axis read downward: people, then the rite, then its source (the palm) and offerings. Scale is small and even; the frame does the enclosing.
panel.narrative: The board may picture an Ifá consultation as a story: a couple (the clients), the diviner tapping the tray, and the oil palm whose nuts give the signs. It is the same theme the Ifá tray EBA-Div_00302 puts on its rim — couples and divination — told as a sequence instead of a ring.
panel.hypotheses: Supports a narrative reading, though of a rite rather than a reign. The ring's ten segments could be tested as a count; nothing else is numerical.
cross_panel_links: Ifá trays and tappers: FoA_04-5598 (four ìróké), FoA_04-5580 and FoA_04-5583 (trays).
Sister plank EBA-Div_00312_panel_01 from the same photograph.
uncertainties: The ring could be a coiled serpent or a drum rather than a tray.
